cases.sentence: Прошло уже три года, как я впервые столкнулся с ___.
cases.explain: «Столкнуться с» ('to bump into someone') takes «с» plus the instrumental, so Семеныч becomes Семенычем.

cases.sentence: Тогда он только еще заступил на ___.
cases.explain: «Заступить на» expresses movement into a position and governs the accusative; должность is inanimate and feminine in -ь, so its accusative looks like the nominative.

cases.sentence: У меня с собой ни ___ нет.
cases.explain: The negative existential «нет», reinforced by «ни», requires the genitive: ни грамма нет.

cases.sentence: Наш поезд, как вкопанный, остановился в ___.
cases.explain: «В» answering «где?» (a place where something happens, not a direction) takes the prepositional case.

cases.sentence: Я ни разу еще не подносил ___ ни единого грамма.
cases.explain: The person given or offered something is the indirect object of «подносить», and indirect objects stand in the dative.
История is the subject of «имеет», and the subject of a sentence stands in the nominative.
The preposition «до» ('as far as, up to') always governs the genitive.

cases.sentence: И женщина Востока сбросит с себя ___!
cases.explain: Паранджа is the direct object of the transitive verb «сбросит», so it takes the accusative: паранджу.

reading.ru: Прошло уже три года, как я впервые столкнулся с Семенычем.
reading.question: How long ago did Venichka first run into Semyonych?
reading.explain: The digression opens by dating their first meeting three years back.

reading.ru: Тогда он только еще заступил на должность.
reading.question: What was Semyonych's situation when they first met?
options: He had only just taken up his post
He had been an inspector for many years
He was travelling as an ordinary passenger
reading.correct: He had only just taken up his post
reading.explain: He was new to the job of ticket inspector at the time.

reading.ru: Я ответил ему, что бить не надо, и промямлил что-то из области римского права.
reading.question: What did Venichka mumble when Semyonych raised the idea of beating him?
options: Something from the field of Roman law
A promise to pay the fine of a hundred and twenty-five
reading.correct: Something from the field of Roman law
reading.explain: Having no vodka and no money, he says beating is unnecessary and mumbles about Roman law instead.

reading.ru: Он страшно заинтересовался и попросил меня рассказать подробнее обо всем античном и римском.
reading.question: How did Semyonych react to the talk of Roman law?
options: He became intensely interested and asked to hear more about antiquity and Rome
He insisted on the hundred and twenty-five roubles
He walked off to the next carriage
reading.correct: He became intensely interested and asked to hear more about antiquity and Rome
reading.explain: His curiosity about ancient history is what saves Venichka from the fine and the beating.

reading.ru: Я от римской истории перешел к христианской и дошел уже до истории с Гипатией.
reading.question: Where had Venichka's storytelling got to at their next meeting?
options: From Roman history to Christian history, as far as Hypatia
To the Golan Heights and Moshe Dayan
reading.correct: From Roman history to Christian history, as far as Hypatia
reading.explain: The serial story moves on from Rome to the Christian era and the fate of Hypatia of Alexandria.

reading.ru: И так продолжалось три года, каждую неделю.
reading.question: How regularly did this arrangement between Venichka and Semyonych repeat?
options: Once a month for a year
reading.explain: The weekly instalment of the story went on for three years running.

reading.ru: В прошлую пятницу я дошел до Индиры Ганди, Моше Даяна и Дубчека.
reading.question: Which figures had the story reached by last Friday?
options: Indira Gandhi, Moshe Dayan and Dubček
reading.correct: Indira Gandhi, Moshe Dayan and Dubček
reading.explain: Having reached contemporary figures, Venichka has run out of history to tell — there is nowhere further to go.

reading.question: What state is Semyonych in during this encounter?
reading.explain: He admits to having drunk a decent amount, and the narrator adds that he was blind drunk.

reading.question: In Venichka's vision of the golden age, what will Diogenes do?
reading.explain: In the coming age there is no more need to search for an honest man, so the lantern goes out.

reading.ru: У публики ведь что сейчас на уме?
reading.question: According to Venichka, what is the one thing on the public's mind nowadays?
reading.explain: He says nothing but homosexuality occupies them, apart from the Arabs, Israel and Moshe Dayan.

reading.ru: Она, эта публика, все поняла не так, как надо было б понять…
reading.question: How did the passengers interpret the scene with Semyonych undressing?
options: They understood it wrongly, not as it should have been understood
They understood exactly what was happening
reading.correct: They understood it wrongly, not as it should have been understood
reading.explain: The sober public leaps up with a huge 'oho' in its eyes, taking the scene the wrong way.

reading.question: Why was it hard for Venichka to move Semyonych?
options: The corridor was blocked by passengers
reading.explain: Softened and unsteady with drink, Semyonych was a monstrous weight to drag.

reading.ru: Я едва дотащил его до тамбура и поставил у входных дверей…
reading.question: Where did Venichka finally get Semyonych to?
options: The vestibule, propped up by the entrance doors
His own seat in the carriage
reading.correct: The vestibule, propped up by the entrance doors
reading.explain: He barely manages to haul him out of sight into the vestibule and stand him by the doors.

reading.ru: Что-нибудь есть у нее под паранджой?..
reading.question: What does Semyonych want to know about the woman of the East?
options: Whether there is anything under her paranja
Whether she will be in Petushki
Why she wears a paranja at all
reading.correct: Whether there is anything under her paranja
reading.explain: His last question is whether anything remains on her once the paranja is thrown off.

reading.question: Why does Semyonych's question go unanswered?
options: The train stopped at Orekhovo-Zuyevo and the door opened
reading.correct: The train stopped at Orekhovo-Zuyevo and the door opened
reading.explain: As always, the stop at Orekhovo-Zuyevo cuts the story off before the answer comes.

highlight.question: Which sentence says where the train stopped and what Semyonych did there?
sentences: И я рассказал ему, что было дальше.
Я от римской истории перешел к христианской и дошел уже до истории с Гипатией.
Я ему говорил: «И вот, по наущению патриарха Кирилла, одержимые фанатизмом монахи Александрии сорвали одежды с прекрасной Гипатии и…»
Но тут наш поезд, как вкопанный, остановился в Орехово-Зуеве, и Семеныч выскочил на перрон, вконец заинтригованный…
highlight.explain: The last sentence is the one that names the station and describes Semyonych jumping out onto the platform.

highlight.question: Which sentence says that Venichka never once gave Semyonych a single gram to drink?
sentences: И так продолжалось три года, каждую неделю.
На линии «Москва – Петушки» я был единственным безбилетником, кто ни разу еще не подносил Семенычу ни единого грамма и тем не менее оставался в живых и непобитых.
Но всякая история имеет конец, и мировая история – тоже…
highlight.explain: The middle sentence describes his unique standing as the fare-dodger who never paid in vodka.

highlight.question: Which sentence says that the public misread what it was seeing?
sentences: Я, как ни был я пьян, поглядел на него с изумлением.
А публика, трезвая публика, почти повскакала с мест, и в десятках глаз ее было написано громадное «ого»!
Она, эта публика, все поняла не так, как надо было б понять…
highlight.explain: The final sentence states outright that the public understood the scene wrongly.

highlight.question: Which sentence gives the setting in which the public sees the two politicians?
sentences: Допустим, смотрят они телевизор: генерал де Голль и Жорж Помпиду встречаются на дипломатическом приеме.
Естественно, оба они улыбаются и руки друг другу жмут.
А уж публика: «Ого! – говорит. – Ай да генерал де Голль!»
highlight.explain: The first sentence supplies the scene — people watching a diplomatic reception on television.

highlight.question: Which sentence says how far Venichka managed to drag Semyonych?
sentences: Я едва дотащил его до тамбура и поставил у входных дверей…
highlight.explain: The third sentence reports that he got him only as far as the vestibule doors.
